The clinical summary presents a highly coherent, ego-syntonic pattern of lifelong social detachment—beginning in early adulthood (with likely earlier roots), persisting non-episodically for ≥2 years, and lacking features of mood, anxiety, or psychotic disorders. Crucially, the patient reports *no subjective distress* about isolation (“I feel ‘okay’”), which strongly argues against depressive, anxious, or adjustment-related explanations. The absence of core ASD features—explicitly denied across multiple domains (pragmatic language, sensory sensitivities, circumscribed interests, social confusion/overload)—and the *lack of corroborating evidence* (e.g., developmental history of peer rejection, childhood aloofness, or formal ASD test scores interpreted clinically) makes ASD *less likely than schizoid personality disorder*, especially given the DSM-5-TR’s emphasis on enduring, pervasive, and ego-syntonic detachment as hallmark of SPD. While ASD cannot be *definitively excluded* due to pending interpretation of standardized measures, the summary explicitly states those tools yielded *no endorsed symptoms* in key domains—and crucially, no functional impairment is reported, nor is there evidence of neurodevelopmental divergence (e.g., language delay, motor clumsiness, academic unevenness). In contrast, every documented feature aligns precisely with DSM-5-TR criteria for Schizoid Personality Disorder: (1) neither desires nor enjoys close relationships; (2) almost always chooses solitary activities; (3) has little, if any, interest in sexual experiences; (4) takes pleasure in few, if any, activities; (5) lacks close friends or confidants; (6) appears indifferent to praise or criticism; (7) shows emotional coldness, detachment, or flattened affect. All seven are implicitly or explicitly supported — and none are contradicted.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Persistent, non-episodic social detachment over ≥2 years  
• Marked preference for solitude and lack of desire for close relationships (including family)  
• Absence of subjective distress about isolation (“I feel ‘okay’”) — consistent with ego-syntonicity  
• No depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, or neurovegetative symptoms (PHQ-9 negative, BDI-II negative)  
• No fear of judgment, anticipatory anxiety, or avoidance driven by fear (GAD-7 = 4, subclinical; no physiological arousal)  
• No psychosis, no ASD-associated features: no sensory sensitivities, no circumscribed interests, no pragmatic language differences, no reported social confusion or overload  
• Onset in early adulthood, with gradual progression suggesting trait-like stability  
• Clinical impression explicitly identifies Schizoid Personality Disorder as primary consideration with supporting features mapped to diagnostic criteria  

[GAPS]  
• Formal interpretation of administered ASD measures (AQ-10, SRS-2, CASI, ADI-R) — pending score integration and clinical correlation  
• Collateral developmental history (e.g., childhood peer relationships, school adaptation, parental report of early sociability)  
• Objective assessment of functional impact (occupational/academic performance, self-care, safety) — noted as “not reported”, not ruled out  
• Physical exam or neurological screening (e.g., for subtle soft signs, motor coordination) — not mentioned, though not required for SPD diagnosis  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Schizoid Personality Disorder
